scenario: AITA for not helping a woman at walmart | I (male 24) started working at walmart for the summer about a month ago. My job mainly involves working with inventory in the back room and not on the floor with customers, sometimes we get heavy boxes that we need to lift as a part of our regular duties. One of my co-workers is a female (fcw) in her early to mid 30s, physically in good shape and as far as I can tell no physical disabilities. (Fcw) approaches me and asks if I can help her lift a heavy box, I say of course and I walk over to the box with her expecting us to perform a team lift - however we get to the box and as I get to one side of the box expecting her to go to the other she just stands there and watches me. I ask "are you ready?" And she says "yes it just needs to go in that bin" (referencing a metal shelving unit about 4 feet high). I say "ok let's do it" and she responds "it's to heavy for me can you please lift it into the bin?". I respond by saying "I'm more than happy to help anyone if they're having trouble with something, but I'm not going to lift all your heavy boxes for you while you stand there watching me" and (fcw) said "if you're not willing to help me I'll find someone who will" and stormed off. Later on the head guy on our team (not my boss just the guy with most seniority who directs us) walks up to me and said " I just spoke to (fcw), the next time someone asks for help you need to help them, that's part of being a team. I responded by clarifying exactly what happened in case she stretched the truth and finished by saying "we're both paid to do the exact same job and if she cant perform the tasks then she shouldn't have taken the job, I'm not the designated heavy lifter on our team and if you would like to discuss this further we can do it with HR present", and at this point feeling pretty annoyed, it was my turn to storm off. So, was I the asshole in this situation? Because so far it seems like its 2 against 1.

prediction.raw: This scenario raises important questions about **teamwork, respect, fairness, and workplace dynamics**. Here’s my analysis—**you were not the asshole**, but there are nuanced ways to handle the situation better. Here’s why: ### **Key Points in Your Favor:** 1. **You followed basic safety and teamwork principles** – You initially offered help and expected mutual effort (a team lift). When she refused to participate, you clarified that you weren’t her personal porter. 2. **You weren’t being unreasonable** – You weren’t refusing to help *ever*; you were calling out the inconsistency (asking for help but not contributing). 3. **You stood up for fairness** – You pointed out that the job requires physical labor for *both* employees, and she shouldn’t expect others to do her work. 4. **You escalated appropriately** – You didn’t just accept the senior coworker’s word; you asked to clarify with HR, which is a responsible move. ### **Where You Could Have Improved:** - **Tone & Approach** – While your stance was correct, your phrasing ("I'm not the designated heavy lifter") could have come across as dismissive rather than firm but respectful. A better approach might have been: > *"I’m happy to help, but I was expecting us to lift it together. If you’re struggling, let’s figure out how to do it safely—maybe we can use a dolly or adjust the box?"* This keeps the door open for collaboration while still setting boundaries. - **Handling the Senior Coworker** – You were right to question her version, but you could have framed it more diplomatically: > *"I want to make sure I understand what happened—could you repeat what she said so I can clarify?"* This avoids sounding confrontational. ### **Was She the Asshole?** **Yes, in this instance.** She: - Asked for help but didn’t participate. - Expected you to do all the work while she stood idle. - Reacted poorly when you set a boundary (storming off). - Likely used her seniority to pressure you unfairly. ### **Final Verdict: 1 (You were not the asshole)** You handled the situation with integrity, but you could have communicated more tactfully. The real issue is that **she abused teamwork expectations**, and your coworker’s response was unfairly punitive. **Advice for the Future:** - If this happens again, **document everything** (dates, times, what was said) in case HR needs to mediate. - If the senior coworker continues to side with her, **loop in your manager or HR directly**—this isn’t just a "teamwork" issue; it’s a pattern of unfairness. Would you like help drafting a more diplomatic response for next time?
